headline: Learned models of protein structure are tested against dynamics and flexibility
label: Protein Structure Dynamics Prediction
summary: Structure predictors and coarse-grained learned models are being checked against NMR dynamics, flexibility, and non-globular conformations.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation of how well structure-based and learned protein models capture conformational dynamics and states beyond a single static fold. A systematic comparison of seven coarse-graining mapping choices for machine-learned protein models finds that resolution and chemical diversity do not always track with one another. AlphaFold predictions are examined against experimentally validated non-globular proteins, where they diverge from biologically relevant structural states. A curated backbone 15N NMR chemical shift dataset benchmarks protein foundation models, with the largest errors in core residues with fast dynamics, supported by MD analysis. ProtFlap predicts residue-level flexibility from static structures using atomic energy features trained on RMSF labels. What is new is benchmarking against experimental dynamical and non-globular observables rather than fold accuracy alone.
